Ben —

Appreciate the materials. Our counsel reviewed the draft and attached an initial redline with comments. High-level points:

1) Transfers: AlphaBio prefers the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) included as the primary transfer mechanism rather than a generic addendum. We need explicit confirmation that SCCs will be executed for each EU customer where required.

2) Subprocessors: We are generally comfortable with a notification model but propose: (a) 45 days' notice for critical subprocessors (hosting, logging); (b) ability to object with defined remediation window.

3) Audit and evidence: For vendors processing EU personal data in the US, we require one of the following: (i) executed SCCs plus a recent SOC 2 Type II report, or (ii) a third-party transfer risk assessment and logging evidence showing data residency controls.

4) Logging & retention: Need a short clause describing retention of audit logs (minimum 90 days) and access procedures for incident investigations.

Please find attached: alpha_dpa_redline_v1.docx with inline counsel comments.

If you can provide a response matrix mapping Redwood's positions to these items, that will help accelerate our internal approvals.

Regards,
Jose
Jose Sanchez
Head of Legal Operations, AlphaBio Therapeutics

Ben / Team —

I reviewed AlphaBio's redline (alpha_dpa_redline_v1.docx). Drafting notes and recommended positions below — I'm attaching a short response matrix to use as the basis for the external reply.

Summary recommendations:
- Transfers / SCCs: Acceptable to confirm that Redwood will execute the EU SCCs for AlphaBio accounts where required. Recommend adding a short clause that SCC execution is per-customer and follows the execution flow (DPA signature triggers SCCs). This is a reasonable concession and avoids negotiating a bespoke addendum.

- Subprocessor notice: Push back on 45 days for all subprocessors. Propose a two-tier model: 30 days notice for standard subprocessors and 45 days for new critical infrastructure providers. That aligns with our current onboarding cadence.

- Audit evidence: We can provide SOC 2 Type II and an attestation of SCCs execution. For customers that need more, offer a scoped transfer risk assessment as an add-on professional-services item.

- Logging retention: 90 days baseline is acceptable, but we should clarify scope (security/audit logs only, not product analytics). Keep remediation window for objections at 30 days with option to suspend services only if material non-remediation.

Escalations to Legal: Clause 7.3 (indemnity carve-outs) and Clause 12 (data export restrictions in narrow regulated sectors) look like items counsel will want to see before final sign-off.

Attachments: response_matrix_draft.docx (use this to reply to AlphaBio counsel).

Naomi
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
